concepts.label: XDCR Replication
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - this is the concept's own defining page. 'An XDCR replication allows data to be replicated continuously from a specified bucket on the source cluster to a specified bucket on the target.' First contact anywhere in the corpus - see xdcr-management-overview.json's own notable_absence for why: neither the reference tree (settings/filtering mechanisms) nor Capella's xdcr.json (topology/conflict-handling vocabulary) ever needed to name the created-object level itself.

concepts.label: XDCR Reference (registered target cluster)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted this batch on create-xdcr-reference.md; every replication requires one already-registered reference as its target

concepts.label: XDCR implicit mapping (keyspace-to-keyspace)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - XDCR's default behavior of replicating between identically-named keyspaces (scope.collection) without an administrator specifying a mapping. 'XDCR's default behavior is always to replicate data between corresponding keyspaces...This is known as replication by _implicit mapping_.' First contact; the fuller definition is on replicate-using-scopes-and-collections.md, this same batch.

relations.subject: xdcr:replication
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (usesEnum) - loose fit: the default behavior is a mode the replication operates in, not a literal enum, matching this project's precedent of loose predicate reuse
relations.evidence: XDCR's default behavior is always to replicate data between corresponding keyspaces: for example, data in `inventory.airline` on the source is replicated to `inventory.airline` on the target.

notable_absence.finding: Unlike create-xdcr-reference.md (this same batch), this page names no role at all for who may create a replication - it silently assumes the Full/Cluster/XDCR Administrator gate already established on the reference-creation page extends to replication creation, but never restates it.

cross_component_finding: ONLY ONE REPLICATION PER TARGET-BUCKET COMBINATION IS A CONSTRAINT NEVER STATED ON THE REFERENCE TREE OR ON CAPELLA'S PAGES. This page's own text ('Note that multiple _replications_...can be created using a single _reference_') implies the constraint is per-reference, not per-bucket-pair, but replicate-using-scopes-and-collections.md (this same batch) later states the sharper rule explicitly: 'XDCR only permits one replication to be defined, for a given target-bucket.' Recorded on that page instead, since this page's own text does not state the restriction, only the multiplicity it does NOT restrict.
